title: US hosted CRM subscription, no services
document_text: Order Form. Vendor grants Customer a non-exclusive, non-transferable right to access the Service during the Subscription Term. The Service is accessed solely through Vendor's hosted platform; no software is delivered or installed. Fees: INR 12,00,000 per year.

Q2.quote: The Service is accessed solely through Vendor's hosted platform

expected.why: Use-only access, treaty documents on file: business profits, no withholding.

title: German on-premise licence plus priced implementation and training
document_text: Licence Agreement. Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual licence to install and use the Software for its internal business purposes only. Licensee shall not copy, modify or distribute the Software. Schedule 2 (Professional Services): Licensor will configure the Software and train Licensee's engineers to administer it independently. Licence fee INR 10,00,000; Professional Services fee INR 4,00,000.

Q1.quote: Licensee shall not copy, modify or distribute the Software

Q2.quote: perpetual licence to install and use the Software

Q3.quote: Licensor will configure the Software and train Licensee's engineers

Q5.quote: train Licensee's engineers to administer it independently

Q6.quote: Licensor will configure the Software and train Licensee's engineers

expected.why: Licence is use-only; services are FTS under a treaty with no make-available test: 10% of 4,00,000.

title: US SaaS plus priced admin training
document_text: Master Order. Customer receives access to the hosted analytics platform for twelve months. Training Services: Vendor will deliver a five-day course so that Customer's staff can build and maintain dashboards without Vendor assistance. Subscription INR 9,00,000; Training Services INR 3,00,000.

Q2.quote: access to the hosted analytics platform

Q3.quote: Vendor will deliver a five-day course

Q5.quote: build and maintain dashboards without Vendor assistance

Q6.quote: Vendor will deliver a five-day course

expected.why: Make-available judgement under the US treaty; tentative FTS at 15% of 3,00,000.

title: Singapore perpetual use-only licence
document_text: End User Licence. Licensor grants Licensee a non-exclusive licence to use one copy of the Software. All intellectual property remains with Licensor and no right to reproduce, adapt or sublicense is granted. Fee INR 20,00,000.

Q1.quote: no right to reproduce, adapt or sublicense is granted

Q2.quote: licence to use one copy of the Software

expected.why: Copyrighted article, not copyright: business profits.

title: UK SDK licence with redistribution rights
document_text: SDK Agreement. Licensor grants Developer the right to modify the SDK and to distribute it, in object code form, embedded in Developer's own products sold to third parties. Fee INR 15,00,000.

Q1.quote: the right to modify the SDK and to distribute it

expected.why: Rights in the copyright itself: royalty at 15%.

title: US SaaS, vendor has not provided a TRC
document_text: Subscription Terms. Customer may access and use the hosted Service for its internal purposes. No copy of any software is provided. Fees INR 8,00,000.

Q2.quote: No copy of any software is provided

expected.why: No TRC: treaty relief unavailable, domestic 20% plus 4% cess = 20.8%.

title: German licence with support bundled, no price split
document_text: Licence and Support Agreement. Licensor grants a licence to use the Software internally. The annual fee of INR 11,00,000 covers the licence, updates and on-call engineering support.

Q2.quote: a licence to use the Software internally

Q4.quote: The annual fee of INR 11,00,000 covers the licence, updates and on-call engineering support

expected.why: Bundled consideration must be split by a human before any rate applies.

title: US implementation partner with consultants on site
document_text: Statement of Work. Vendor will station two consultants at Customer's Bengaluru office for four months to implement the platform. Fees INR 25,00,000.

Q7.quote: station two consultants at Customer's Bengaluru office for four months

expected.why: Possible service PE: needs a specialist before any treaty article is applied.

title: Singapore SaaS where the model invents a sublicensing clause
document_text: Terms of Service. Customer may use the hosted Service for its own internal operations. Customer may not resell or sublicense access. Fees INR 6,00,000.

Q1.quote: Customer may sublicense the Software to its affiliates

Q2.quote: use the hosted Service for its own internal operations

expected.why: Fabricated quote is caught by the quote check; Q1 is left unresolved.

title: Irish vendor, treaty not in the rules table
document_text: Subscription Agreement. Customer may access the hosted Service. Fees INR 6,00,000.

Q2.quote: Customer may access the hosted Service

expected.why: The system refuses to guess a treaty it has no rules for.

title: German consulting where the payer bears the tax
document_text: Consulting Agreement. Consultant will advise Client on its data-platform architecture. All fees are payable net of any Indian taxes, which Client shall bear. Fees INR 9,00,000.

Q3.quote: Consultant will advise Client on its data-platform architecture

Q6.quote: Consultant will advise Client on its data-platform architecture

title: US order form relying on an unseen master agreement
document_text: Order Form No. 7. Licence scope, usage rights and restrictions are as set out in the Master Subscription Agreement. Fees INR 7,00,000.

Q8.quote: as set out in the Master Subscription Agreement

expected.why: The deciding clause is in a document nobody uploaded.

title: US SaaS where the samples disagree on delivery
document_text: Subscription. Customer may use the cloud Service and may download a desktop connector for convenience. Fees INR 10,00,000.

expected.why: Disagreement is surfaced to a human, though it does not change the category here.

title: Singapore training sessions below the Form 146 threshold
document_text: Services Order. Vendor will run two workshops teaching Customer's analysts to build forecasting models on their own. Fees INR 3,00,000.

Q5.quote: teaching Customer's analysts to build forecasting models on their own

expected.why: Make-available case (specialist); tentative 10%; aggregate under 5 lakh so Part A, no CA certificate.

title: DESIGNED FAILURE: US model API plus a licensed training dataset
document_text: API and Data Agreement. Customer may call the hosted model through the API. Provider also licenses the Benchmark Dataset to Customer, which Customer may download and use to train its own internal models. Fees INR 18,00,000.

Q2.quote: Customer may call the hosted model through the API

expected.why: A dataset licence raises a royalty question the checklist never asks. Expected to FAIL: shows the weakest point.

title: DESIGNED FAILURE: Singapore SaaS with routine email support bundled
document_text: Subscription. Customer may access the hosted Service. Standard email support during business hours is included in the fee. Fees INR 7,00,000.

Q2.quote: Customer may access the hosted Service

Q3.quote: Standard email support during business hours is included in the fee

expected.why: Routine support is incidental to the subscription. Expected to FAIL: the bundling rule over-escalates.
